**Description**
AWS runs one of the largest networks in the world. We design and implement its network devices and their operating system, NetOS. Every AWS service runs on this network, and every packet in the cloud touches our code! Nobody notices a healthy network. Operators need to know within seconds when a link degrades in one data center, and the first signal comes from software on the device. We write that software.
  
  
Our team, NetOS Observability, builds the agent that collects metrics, events, and logs from every NetOS device and publishes them to the network telemetry platform. Fleet health systems, SDN controllers, and network operators consume what we ship.
  
  
We are moving the fleet off a legacy daemon and onto a brand new Rust agent. In 2027, we take it to every supported platform, retire the legacy collectors, and let builders publish a new metric fleet-wide in two weeks. You will own that agent end to end, from its design to its release across the fleet to its behavior in production. The decisions that shape the next decade of network telemetry are open now. We need your help to craft the future.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  

* Design and implement the NetOS observability agent in Rust on Linux (ARM64).
* Own the telemetry pipeline from device to gateway, including transport, authentication, schema, backpressure, and fleet-scale correctness.
* Migrate consumers off the legacy daemon with adapters that preserve their data shape, then retire the daemon.
* Build the test and release machinery that ships the component to the fleet on its own cadence. Every release passes its test gate.
* Instrument your own systems, define their SLOs, and carry the on-call rotation for them.
* Write design documents and review other engineers' designs. Name the dependency early when another team's roadmap gates yours, and negotiate the date.

A day in the life
  
  
You write Rust and test on real routers in our lab. You build for the component teams who define their telemetry in a schema we own, and for the fleet health systems, controllers, and operators who consume it. Every two weeks you settle the device-to-cloud contract with the telemetry platform team. You add a metric to the schema, bring a legacy consumer onto the new pipeline, and run the result on a router under its memory budget. AI agents draft, review, and test alongside you. You ship the component every few weeks and carry its on-call.
  
  
**About The Team**
Our team sits inside NetOS Managed Fleet, which delivers health, observability, and management services for the NetOS fleet. We are growing the team in Raleigh, NC. You work directly with senior engineers and leadership across AWS Networking, and you give technical guidance as the team grows. We own what we ship, and we carry the on-call for the agent in production. We value clear design writing, incremental delivery, and property-based tests.

**Description**
At Amazon Web Services (AWS), we are at the forefront of cloud computing, providing services that power millions of customers worldwide. Our Threat Intelligence team plays a critical role in protecting AWS infrastructure and our customers from sophisticated threats. We are seeking an Applied Scientist to join our team and help develop AI/ML models that detect and mitigate threat activities targeting AWS services and customers.
  
  
AWS Identity Threat Detection protects every door into AWS. Our Threat Evaluation Service (TES) sits inline on the authentication and registration paths for hundreds of millions of identities — from root account sign-in to Builder ID creation to OAuth token issuance — making sub-100ms fraud decisions at thousands of requests per second across multiple regions.
  
  
As an Applied Scientist on our team, you will work at the intersection of artificial intelligence, machine learning, cybersecurity, and threat intelligence. You will collaborate with security engineers, software engineers, and threat researchers to build innovative solutions that identify patterns of suspicious behavior across vast amounts of network data. Your work will directly contribute to the security posture of AWS and help protect our customers from emerging threats.
  
  
In this role, you will apply your analytical expertise to deeply understand the threat landscape affecting cloud environments. You will develop a comprehensive understanding of threat actor techniques, tactics, and procedures and translate this knowledge into effective detection models. By analyzing network signals and traffic patterns, you will help produce actionable threat intelligence that enables our engineering teams to implement robust defenses against sophisticated actors.
  
  
Your responsibilities will include designing and implementing machine learning algorithms that can process and analyze large-scale network data in real-time. You will work with diverse data sources, including network logs, API calls, and system telemetry, to identify anomalous patterns indicative of malicious activity. Through continuous refinement of your models, you will help reduce false positives while ensuring high detection rates for genuine threats.
  
  
The ideal candidate possesses mathematical and statistical foundations, with experience applying machine learning techniques to complex problems. You should have a track record of developing and deploying ML models in production environments, preferably in the security domain. Proficiency in programming languages such as Python is preferred, along with experience using common AI/ML frameworks and tools.
  
  
Beyond technical skills, you should demonstrate analytical thinking and problem-solving abilities. The threat landscape is constantly evolving, requiring you to adapt your approaches and develop novel solutions to counter new traffic vectors. Your curiosity and passion for understanding adversarial behaviors will drive you to continuously improve our detection capabilities. Collaboration is key in this role, as you will work closely with cross-functional teams to translate your research into practical security solutions. **Description**
Training and running large AI models takes enormous amounts of expensive accelerated compute, and most of it sits idle. Across the industry, a large share of GPU capacity is paid for but never does useful work because jobs cannot find it, cannot share it, or cannot see it and use it efficiently. We build the services that closes that gap.
  
  
We are looking for a Software Development Engineer to help build the systems that put idle or inefficiently used GPUs to work. You will design and build distributed backend services that let organizations pool capacity across many clusters and accounts, route it to the workloads that need it most, and see exactly how it is being used. This is deep systems work at the intersection of large-scale distributed systems, container orchestration, and cloud infrastructure, and it directly changes how much value customers get from every GPU they pay for.
  
  
You will own services end to end, from design through launch and operation in production, and your work will ship to some of the largest AI compute customers in the world.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  
Design, build, and operate distributed backend services that manage and share accelerated compute across multiple clusters and accounts.
  
  
Build scheduling and capacity-sharing capabilities that move compute to the highest-priority workloads and reclaim it when priorities change.
  
  
Build zero-touch usage and guidance systems that collect, aggregate, and report how compute is consumed, at scale and in near real time.
  
  
Own your services in production: define operational metrics, respond to issues, and continuously improve reliability, latency, and cost.
  
  
Write clear design documents, participate in design and code reviews, and raise the engineering bar for the team.
  
  
Collaborate with product, design, and partner engineering teams to turn customer problems into shipped features.
  
  
Mentor other engineers and contribute to a culture of ownership, quality, and customer focus.
  
  
A day in the life
  
  
Most days start with a short team stand-up, then it is mostly building. You might design a service that lets one cluster borrow idle capacity from another, then write it up for a design review where the team pokes holes in it before any code is written. Hard problems get their own deep-dive whiteboard session. Other days lean toward operations, chasing down why a workload did not get the capacity it should have. You will not be handed fully specified tasks; you will have the independence to help decide what to build, then build it.
  
  
**About The Team**
We help customers get the most out of the accelerated compute they pay for. Our mission is simple to say and hard to do: make sure every accelerator a customer pays for is doing useful work, and make that easy to see and control. Cost reduction is one important part of that, but the bigger idea is the engine that delivers compute to the workloads that need it most, in as little time as possible.
  
  
Our customers run some of the largest AI training and inference workloads in the world, and they feel the impact of our work directly in how much they can do with their infrastructure. We care about depth, we own our work end to end, and we build in the open where we can.

**About Clarion**
Clarion is the first system built to run the whole medical practice. Revenue is up 10x in a year, we have eight-figure contracted revenue, and this fall we signed the two largest contracts in our history. We're a team of 20, and the people who join now will define what Clarion becomes.
  
  
**Medical practices are at a breaking point**
Reimbursement is falling, costs are rising, and patients are falling through the cracks.
  
  

* Medicare pays practices 33% less than it did in 2001, after adjusting for practice costs (AMA).
* 84% of practices say operating costs are up again this year. Fewer than half say revenue is (MGMA).
* In one large health system, only 35% of specialist referrals ended in a completed visit (Journal of General Internal Medicine).

**What We Do**
Every practice runs on rules that live in schedulers' heads and on sticky notes behind the front desk. We take the time to learn those rules. Then our AI agents follow them to handle calls, referrals, and scheduling for specialty groups and value-based care organizations, and document the work in the EHR. Staff get their time back for the work that needs a person.
  
  
**Where we're going**
We're building a new category of software, the practice operations platform, or POP. It's the biggest shift in how practices run since the EHR.
  
  
Within a few years, we believe every practice will run on just two systems. One is the electronic health record. The other is a practice operations platform, where AI agents handle the tasks people do by hand in the clinic today, from the first phone call to the final payment. The EHR is the source of truth for patient care. Clarion will be the source of truth for running the practice.
  
  
We started with calls, referrals, and scheduling. Billing, prior auth, and collections come next. We want Clarion to be as essential to every practice as its EHR, and we're hiring the people who will build it.
  
  
**Why join now**

* Early, but de-risked. Revenue is up 10x year over year and we have eight-figure contracted revenue. Most of our growth for the next two quarters is already signed.
* We win the biggest deals. This fall we signed the two largest contracts in our history. One is a three-year enterprise agreement with one of the largest GI groups in the country, won after a 15-vendor RFP and a head-to-head pilot. We win 80% of competitive head-to-head deals. Our customers also include a Fortune 500 payor and two of the five largest ACOs in the country.
* The product works. Our AI agents handle more than 10 million patient calls a year for our customers. They resolve 60% of in-scope calls end to end and convert 70% of the referrals they work into booked visits.
* We move fast. We launched 345 providers in Q3, three times the quarter before, and our fastest kickoff to go-live is under five days. Our customers span nearly 1,500 locations and more than 3,700 providers across 18 specialties.
* The team. Clarion was founded by Ryan Gallagher, a Stanford- and Harvard-trained doctor on the founding team of two successful virtual care companies, and Jeff Lamothe, an ex-Amazon Alexa engineer who led AI/ML teams at Salesforce. We've raised $10M from Accel and Y Combinator, and the 20 of us work in person in Flatiron.

**Why this role**

* Real ownership, early. We're a team of 20. You'll own features and systems used every day in real practices.
* Real scale. Our agents handle more than 10 million patient calls a year, so what you ship gets tested by real volume.
* Learn from experienced builders. You'll work with our CTO, our Head of Engineering, and senior engineers on AI, real-time systems, and healthcare integrations.

**What You'll Do**

* Build and operate production full-stack features for Clarion's AI agents.
* Integrate with EHRs, legacy healthcare systems, and real-time voice infrastructure.
* Work with product, design, and senior engineers to turn customer needs into shipped software.
* Debug and improve reliability, performance, and scalability across live systems.
* Contribute to technical discussions, code reviews, and engineering practices.

**Interesting technical challenges**

* AI-powered workflows. Support and extend LLM-driven systems used in real-time healthcare interactions.

* Healthcare integrations. Build resilient abstractions across fragmented, regulated systems while maintaining security and compliance.

**What We're Looking For**

* A strong sense of ownership. You care about quality, reliability, and real-world impact.

* Direct access. You'll work with our CTO and Head of Engineering every day, so decisions are fast and ownership is real.

The next quant firm is a learning system. We’re building an investment firm around an AI researcher that tests investment ideas and carries what it learns into the next experiment.
  
  
We’re a team of researchers and engineers in New York, and we work in person. We’re curious about how things work, quick to put ideas to the test, and willing to question our own assumptions. Build the researcher with us.
  
  
**The Role**
You will build the research platform behind our AI researcher. The AI researcher implements and tests signals, and you build and own everything it relies on: the backtesting engine, the data pipelines that feed it, the tooling that evaluates results, and the path from research to live trading. You'll work directly with researchers and engineers to decide what the platform should do, and you'll ship without waiting for a perfect spec. The AI researcher runs experiments around the clock, so the backtester is the referee, and a referee has to be fast, correct, and very hard to fool.
  
  
As a member of the founding team, you'll directly impact every level of the business, from product strategy to team culture.
  
  
**What You'll Do**

* Work directly with researchers and engineers to build the platform our AI researcher uses to turn ideas into signals: the signal framework, reusable feature and model components, and experiment tracking
* Build and own the backtesting engine and the research APIs that researchers, engineers, and agents build on: walk-forward simulation, realistic fills and transaction costs, portfolio construction, and results that reproduce exactly
* Build and run the pipelines for our large financial datasets. Ingest messy vendor feeds, validate them, store them point-in-time, and get corporate actions, delistings, and security identity right across US equities. Make every dataset easy to find and hard to misuse
* Develop the evaluation tooling that decides whether an idea is real: signal diagnostics, risk attribution, statistical tests, and automated checks that catch look-ahead, leakage, and bugs in agent-written code before anyone trusts a result
* Ship to production and own what you ship: deployment, monitoring, and reconciliation of live trading against the backtest, in systems where mistakes cost real money
* Profile and speed up heavy numerical workloads so the loop from idea to evidence takes minutes, not hours

**What We're Looking For**

* At least 2 years building research or trading systems at a quant fund, trading firm, or systematic investment team, or equivalent depth shown through shipped systems
* Expert-level Python and deep fluency in its numeric stack (NumPy, pandas or Polars, SciPy), with strong engineering fundamentals: testing, debugging, profiling, and writing code other people can build on
* Experience building pipelines over large financial datasets, especially US equities: vendor feeds, point-in-time fundamentals, corporate actions, and symbology
* Hands-on experience building or maintaining a backtester, and a clear understanding of the systematic investment process: signals, risk models, portfolio construction, and transaction costs
* A solid grounding in statistics and working knowledge of machine learning: enough to get the platform's math right and to notice when the numbers don't add up
* Experience working directly with researchers and engineers, building the tools they depend on. You can take a half-formed request, ask the questions that pin it down, and turn it into a system they trust
* You default to shipping. Given ambiguity, you produce a working system and iterate, rather than waiting for requirements to firm up
* Low ego, high standards, fast execution

**Compensation**

Our agents have supported more than 10 million patient encounters and are on track to grow tenfold this year. As a Software Engineer, Voice Evaluation at Concurrence, you'll build the system that determines whether a voice agent is ready for patients. You'll own realistic audio tests, scoring and the release gate, with authority to block releases that fail it. The tests need to catch failures that a clean transcript can miss, from mishandled interruptions to missed clinical information or a failure to hand off to a person.
  
  
**What You'll Do**

* Build simulated callers and call-replay tests that exercise the production voice path with real audio
* Test phone trees, hold queues, interruptions, conflicting clinical information and appropriate escalation
* Build scoring systems and calibrate automated judges against human assessments
* Measure clinical failure rates and uncertainty, and test whether simulation results predict behavior on real calls
* Define release criteria with model, runtime, product and clinical colleagues, own the gate and block changes that fail those criteria
* Turn production failures into regression tests, verify fixes and monitor behavior after release
* Maintain held-out evaluation sets so models are tested on examples they did not train against

**What We're Looking For**

* You've personally built and owned evaluation or simulation for production agents at scale. Voice and audio experience is a strong preference
* You've built agent simulations or replay systems, implemented scoring and caught a concrete failure before release
* Your evaluation results determined what shipped, and you led that work

* You write reliable software that runs at volume and follow failures through to a verified fix
* You use coding agents in your work and independently verify their output

Underneath our platform is the Health World Model, which unifies a health system’s data into a living, event-level record of every patient’s care. On top of it, agents handle work across the patient journey, from intake and scheduling to medication management and clinical decision support.
  
  
Our agents have supported more than 10 million patient encounters and are on track to grow tenfold this year. We run natively on Databricks, integrate with every major EHR, and are backed by Madrona, General Catalyst, and Optum Ventures. We’re about 35 people, working in person in New York and San Francisco.
  
  
**About This Role**
As a Research Engineer, Voice AI at Concurrence, you'll build and tune speech models for patient conversations and ambient clinical audio. You'll own models from data and training through evaluation and production, working with runtime engineers on streaming inference, latency and turn-taking. The work includes full-duplex speech-to-speech models that listen and speak at the same time, handle interruptions and preserve clinical details.
  
  
**What You'll Do**

* Train and fine-tune speech and audio models for patient calls and clinical encounters
* Own data preparation, training experiments and evaluation code
* Improve streaming inference, turn-taking and interruption handling, balancing model quality, latency and cost
* Define clinical failure cases with clinicians, product and evaluation engineers, and measure the errors that matter to patients
* Evaluate changes on held-out examples, investigate regressions and carry improvements into production
* Use evidence from real conversations to choose the next experiment and shape our modeling approach

**What we're looking for**

* You've personally trained or fine-tuned speech or audio models on large audio datasets as a substantial part of your work
* You've shipped a model into a real-time product, with concrete results on streaming inference, latency, turn-taking or overlapping speech
* You've taken an ambiguous problem, defined a useful metric and led the work through to a model running in production
* You write the training and evaluation code yourself and can explain the choices behind an experiment
* You use coding agents in your work and independently verify their output
* You're low ego, direct, and hold yourself to a high bar
* You can work on site in New York City or San Francisco

**Nice to have**

* Experience building or tuning a full-duplex speech-to-speech model, our strongest preference
* Neural audio codecs or audio language models
* Telephone audio, overlapping speech or multi-speaker audio
* Model adaptation for a particular customer, domain or regulated environment

**Health & Wellness**

* Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance
* Daily catered lunch and dinner
* Mental health support and wellness coaching
* Flexible wellness stipend for fitness, therapy, or personal growth

**Growth & Development**

* Annual learning budget for courses, books, or conferences
* Conference attendance budget for professional development
* Annual team offsite
* Academic collaboration opportunities
* Unlimited PTO

**Our Core Values**

* Patients Win, We Win

If patients aren't getting better care, we haven't earned the right to scale. Every internal decision gets pressure-tested: does this make patients' lives better? If we can't draw the line, we question why we're doing it.
  
  

* High Standards, High Care

We hold a high bar for the team because patients are counting on us to get this right. But high standards only work with genuine investment in each other. You can take risks, admit mistakes, and challenge ideas. Not despite our standards, but because of them.
  
  

* Thoughtful Urgency

We move fast by default, but speed without judgment is recklessness. The discipline is knowing which decisions are reversible vs. not. In healthcare AI, the companies that win will be fast everywhere they can be and careful everywhere they must be. We build the muscle to do both.
  
  

* Intensely Measured

We instrument patient outcomes, provider ROI, system performance, and clinical accuracy. But data without action is surveillance. Every metric should have an owner, a threshold, and a response plan. If we're measuring something but never acting on it, we stop measuring it.
**Who Builds With Us**

* Low ego: Politics and territory don't interest you. The best ideas win, regardless of who has them.
* Direct: You say the hard thing, challenge ideas openly, and commit fully once decided.
* High agency: You thrive on trust rather than instruction. When you see something is broken, you fix it. You don’t file tickets and wait for someone else.
* Bar of excellence: You hold yourself to a bar most people wouldn't, and you want teammates who do the same.
* Skeptical: You push back on rules that don’t make sense and question assumptions that haven’t earned their place.

* Experience with Snowflake Cortex services such as Cortex Agents, Cortex Analyst, and Cortex AI Functions; familiarity with Snowflake CoCo for AI-assisted development.

**Description**
Do you want to shape the future of virtualized networking in one of the world's largest public clouds?
  
  
The Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) NX Platforms team owns the packet processing pipeline running beneath every EC2 instance — adding encryption, firewalls (security groups), routing, billing, and monitoring to every packet on every host across our worldwide fleet of 9M+ hosts in more than 30 regions. Our vision: deliver bare-metal networking performance while raising the bar on EC2's security, availability, and reliability — unlocking capabilities only possible through true Software Defined Networking (SDN).
  
  
We are growing fast and looking for senior systems engineers who can deliver ultra-high performance — our goal is processing millions of packets per second on a single CPU core. This demands highly optimized data structures, low-level hardware tuning, and expertise in C/C++. If you have a passion for systems software engineering — kernel development, embedded systems, or high-performance networking — this is a unique opportunity to define the next generation of the platform powering all new EC2 instance families and VPC features for years to come.
  
  
Your code ships to production across the entire EC2 fleet — powering services like AWS Lambda and every external workload running on EC2. With frequent deployments and full ownership from design through operation, your contributions have immediate, measurable impact at global scale.
  
  
With an extensive network and access to Principal, Sr. Principal, and Distinguished Engineers across EC2, AWS, and Amazon, there are many stretch opportunities to grow your skills and knowledge.
  
  
Ready to build the networking substrate for the world's largest cloud? Apply today.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  

* Own the end-to-end design, scoping, implementation, and integration testing of new features that run on the EC2 Nitro System.
* Design and build secure and scalable services to enable monitoring, diagnostics, and automated recovery.
* Design and build next generation hardware/software validation platforms that enables efficient CI/CD.
* Collaborate with cross-functional teams to understand and define requirements, design system architectures, and implement robust and scalable solutions.
* Continuously improve development processes, tools, and automation to enhance productivity and quality.
* Mentor junior engineers with scoping, design, and developing scalable and maintainable code.

**About The Team**

* Why AWS

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.
  
  

* Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.
